ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, and CD is a chord with AB $\perp$ CD at point E. Connect AC, OC, and BC. If AE = 2cm and BE = 8cm, what is the length of chord CD in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $AE=2\text{cm}$ and $BE=8\text{cm}$,\\
it follows that $OA=5\text{cm}$ and $OE=3\text{cm}$,\\
In $\triangle OCE$, $CE= \sqrt{5^2-3^2}=4\text{cm}$,\\
Since $AB\perp CD$,\\
it implies $CE=DE$,\\
Therefore, $CD=2CE=\boxed{8\text{cm}}$;

method.method_draft: Use the center-radius right triangle route. First read the diagram: AB is the horizontal diameter of the circle with center O, E lies on AB between A and O, and chord CD crosses AB perpendicularly at E with C above and D below. From the text, AE=2 cm and BE=8 cm, so AB=10 cm and the radius OA=OC=5 cm. Since E is 2 cm from A and O is the midpoint of AB, OE=5-2=3 cm. Because AB is perpendicular to CD, triangle OCE is right at E. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: CE=sqrt(OC^2-OE^2)=sqrt(25-9)=4. Since a perpendicular from the circle center to a chord bisects the chord, CE=DE, so CD=2CE=8 cm.
